advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm reconverge's remote/branch resolution source matches _pin_tickets_sha's confirm-step source, or document why they cannot diverge.
evidence: sync.py:228 `remote_name = tickets_remote(os.path.dirname(str(tracker)))` — reconverge derives remote from the tracker's parent, not root_dir
ABSENCE: no assertion or comment that these two resolution sources are guaranteed identical
advisory.finding: In `_pin_tickets_sha` (fetch=True), the `merge-base --is-ancestor` confirm uses `{remote}/{branch}` resolved from `root_dir`, while `reconverge(tracker)` independently resolves its remote/branch from the tracker's parent dir (`os.path.dirname(tracker)`). These coincide in the normal layout, but if the tracker's parent config and root_dir config ever diverge (e.g. a non-default `tickets_remote`/`tickets_branch` in one but not the other), the fetched remote-tracking ref (`{remote_name}/{branch}`) and the confirmed ref (`{remote}/{branch}`) would differ, causing a spurious fall-back to the direct origin/tickets pin. Not a correctness bug (fall-back is safe) but a latent inconsistency in the freshness path.
scenarios: A checkout where the tracker's parent-dir config and the passed root_dir config resolve different tickets_remote/tickets_branch values

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update docs/exit-codes.md:193 so the verify-completion exit-11 entry documents the new 'no verdict obtainable' verifier-FAULT path (not only the raised-LLMError 'shape B' case).
evidence: src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:325: `if result.get("verdict_obtainable") is False:` then `return 11` — reached on the normal verify_completion return path, NOT via the raised-LLMError branch (`_llm_error_exit_code`, lines 309-312).

docs/exit-codes.md:193: `| verify-completion | 0 | 1 | — | PASS → 0, FAIL → 1, retryable degrade → 11 (shape B — raised `LLMError`) |` — the parenthetical scopes exit 11 to a raised LLMError only; the new verdict-in-hand fault path is not covered.
docs/exit-codes.md is not among the 12 changed files, so the contract table was not updated for the new exit-11 condition.
advisory.finding: `rebar verify-completion` now returns exit 11 from the normal reconciled-verdict path when `verdict_obtainable is False` (a verifier FAULT), but the frozen exit-code contract doc still describes exit 11 for this verb as arising only from a raised LLMError ('shape B'), so the CLI exit-code contract documentation understates the new exit-11 condition.
scenarios: A caller scripting `rebar verify-completion` and consulting docs/exit-codes.md expects exit 11 only on a raised LLM outage; a garbled/truncated verifier turn now also returns 11 with no documented explanation of that path.
advisory.suggested_fix: Amend the verify-completion row in docs/exit-codes.md to note exit 11 also fires on a reconciled verifier FAULT (`verdict_obtainable=false`, bug 2a6f), not only on a raised retryable LLMError.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a `verify-completion` CLI facade test that monkeypatches verify_completion to return `verdict_obtainable=False` and asserts `main([...]) == 11`.
evidence: Diff adds: `if result.get("verdict_obtainable") is False:\n        return 11`
search 'verdict_obtainable' in tests returns only test_completion_verifier.py and test_no_verdict_obtainable_2a6f.py — no CLI facade hit

tests/interfaces/facades/test_verify_completion_facades.py:133-139 `test_cli_fail_exits_one` asserts rc == 1 with a _fail fixture that has no verdict_obtainable marker; no analogous exit-11 test exists
advisory.finding: The new CLI exit-11 disposition for a verifier FAULT (`if result.get("verdict_obtainable") is False: return 11`) has no test. The facade suite asserts exit 0 (PASS) and exit 1 (FAIL) but never the new exit 11, so a regression that flattens the fault back into exit 1 (the exact pre-fix behavior the diff calls out) would not be caught.
scenarios: A refactor or regression drops the exit-11 branch and a fault reverts to exit 1; automation scripting `verify-completion` treats a transient verifier fault as a criteria-unmet FAIL
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `test_cli_no_verdict_obtainable_exits_eleven` mirroring `test_cli_fail_exits_one` but with a fake returning `{"verdict": "FAIL", "verdict_obtainable": False, "findings": [...]}` and assert rc == 11.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a close_precheck/close-gate test that drives the completion verifier to return `verdict_obtainable=False` and asserts a CommandError with returncode=11 and the fault message (and that the ticket does not close).
evidence: Diff adds `_raise_on_verifier_fault(...)` raising `CommandError(..., returncode=11)` and its invocation in `_completion_precheck`
advisory.finding: The new close-gate fault path `_raise_on_verifier_fault` (raises CommandError with returncode=11 and a distinct 're-run the close' message when `verdict_obtainable` is False) has no test. This is the primary consumer the diff describes ('Same disposition the close gate gives it'), yet no test exercises the close precheck reaching this branch.
scenarios: A verifier returns a fault during a close; a regression stops the raise or changes the returncode so the close reports a fabricated unmet criterion or the wrong exit code, undetected
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_verify_completion_facades.py (which has `_enable_close_gate`/`_seed_in_progress` helpers) add a close-gate test with a fake verdict carrying `verdict_obtainable=False` and assert the close is refused with exit 11.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the getsource substring assertion with a behavioral test that invokes `gate_ops.completion_reconcile` on a bare-FAIL StepContext and asserts the resulting verdict carries `verdict_obtainable is False`.
evidence: The test docstring itself says 'assert it actually inherits the marker rather than assuming delegation' — but grepping the source is assuming delegation via text, not observing the inherited marker
gate_ops.completion_reconcile exists at src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:251 and could be invoked to assert the marker on its output
advisory.finding: `test_workflow_path_inherits_the_marker` asserts on the TEXT of the source under test (`inspect.getsource(gate_ops.completion_reconcile)` then `assert "reconcile_verdict(result)" in src`) instead of exercising behavior. It is a source-grepping change-detector: it breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. `reconcile_verdict(result=result)`, an alias, or an extracted helper) and cannot detect a regression where the marker fails to propagate through the workflow path.
scenarios: completion_reconcile is refactored to call reconcile_verdict differently or via a wrapper; the test breaks with no behavior change, or conversely passes while marker propagation silently regresses
advisory.suggested_fix: Construct a StepContext with a bare FAIL result, call `completion_reconcile`, and assert the returned/mutated result has `verdict_obtainable is False`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where the tracker HEAD is behind `origin/tickets` (confirm fails) and assert the pin falls back to the direct `origin/tickets` chain and the resulting snapshot still holds the origin-only content.
evidence: Diff: `if probe.returncode != 0:\n            return None` after the `merge-base --is-ancestor` probe
tests/interfaces/store/test_gate_ticket_snapshot.py test_fetch_true_pin_loses_nothing_that_origin_holds only exercises the reconverge-then-confirm SUCCESS path (peer content pulled in and present)
No test constructs a tracker whose HEAD is behind origin such that --is-ancestor fails, to assert the direct origin/tickets fallback still yields the origin content
advisory.finding: The `fetch=True` fallback branch of `_pin_tickets_sha` — where `merge-base --is-ancestor` returns non-zero (HEAD not confirmed at-or-ahead of `<remote>/<branch>`) so the function returns None and the caller falls back to the direct `origin/tickets` pin — is not exercised by any test. The two fetch=True tests cover the confirmed-HEAD case and the trackerless-None case, but not the unconfirmable-HEAD fallback the docstring emphasizes ('falling back to today's exact behaviour').
scenarios: A tracker HEAD that cannot be confirmed at-or-ahead of the shared ref; a regression in the fallback would silently pin a store missing content the shared ref holds — the exact invariant the change promises to protect
